editorial:
Imagine you are a successful writer named Yoshiko who spends her days reading fan mail. Everything seems normal until you find a letter from a man who claims he is too ugly to be seen by anyone. He is a lonely chair maker who has a very strange obsession with his work. He tells you that he doesn't have any friends or family, but he has a dark secret about how he spends his time. The movie creates a creepy, quiet mood that makes you feel like something bad is about to happen right under your nose.

You will probably love the slow build-up and the way the mystery unfolds. The acting is solid, though the slow speed might bore some people who want constant action. If you like stories that mess with your head, you should definitely check this one out. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a high-quality 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to see if you enjoy this kind of weird, dark drama.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the chair maker has built a special chair with a hollow space inside it. He hides himself inside the chair and sells it to Yoshiko. For a long time, he stays hidden inside the furniture while she sits on him, listening to her life. In the end, he is finally discovered, revealing the shocking and gross truth about his plan to be close to her without being seen.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and strange plot twists.
